title: Jerusalem artichoke and carrot soup with goat's cheese

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Butter, onion, garlic, artichokes, carrots, stock, milk, goat's cheese and pumpkin seeds are all ordinary kitchen foods, with no jars or packet products.

supermarket.reason: Jerusalem artichokes are the set hero and appear seasonally in larger supermarkets, and everything else is everyday stock at an everyday price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large pan and a stick blender for soup, both allowed, and the technique is simple.

works.reason: About 850g of vegetables in 1 litre of stock plus 200ml milk, simmered 25 minutes and blended, gives a sensible soup for four, finished with cheese and toasted seeds.

honest_times.reason: Scrubbing and slicing 500g of artichokes, chopping the rest and toasting the seeds fits in about 15 minutes, and the 5 minutes softening plus 25 minutes simmering matches the 30 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the thyme, salt and pepper, is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot, earthy artichoke soup suits 1 November, and the artichokes are the body of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a vegetable-rich soup with cheese and seeds, a proper lunch a family would happily eat again.
